<!-- generated from maestro item 1209 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
Every django-mojo deployment can report incidents and tickets into one central
Maestro workspace at maestromojo.com. Because that relationship is singular and
deployment-wide, its workspace reporting ApiKey is static deployment
configuration in `django.conf`, not a database model. Individual reports may
select a remote board; Maestro routes reports without a board to the
integration's configured default.

---

## Spec

Agent-facing from here down. **Kind**: feature · **Requested by**: Ian Starnes

### Product Contract

- A Maestro workspace admin creates one django-mojo project integration, chooses
  its default board, and copies its reporting ApiKey. The django deployment's
  registration command supplies the callback target derived from its public URL.
- The django-mojo deployment sets `MAESTRO_API_KEY` in `django.conf` once.
  `MAESTRO_API_URL` defaults to `https://maestromojo.com` and is overrideable for
  development/self-hosting; no credential-bearing connection row or setup CRUD
  exists locally.
- The ApiKey identifies the remote workspace and source integration, is sent as
  `Authorization: apikey <token>`, and is not pinned to one board.
- `board=<id>` always means a **remote Maestro board id** in the key's workspace.
  Maestro validates that boundary. Omitting `board` uses the integration's
  server-side default board.
- `maestro://?board=3` reports the Incident itself and creates no local Ticket;
  `maestro://` reports to the default board.
- `ticket://?...&board=3` creates/reuses a local Ticket and reports that Ticket
  to remote board 3. `ticket://?...&maestro=1` reports to the default; plain
  `ticket://?...` remains local-only.
- An existing Ticket exposes `push_to_maestro`: `true` uses the default and a
  strict positive integer selects that remote board. Re-pushing is idempotent.
- A Maestro item remains owned by its source integration key but can be triaged
  or moved to any board inside the workspace without breaking the local link.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Runtime configuration reads `MAESTRO_API_KEY` and `MAESTRO_API_URL` only
      through the project settings helper as static settings. Missing config is
      reported by name without logging or serializing the secret.
- [ ] No active runtime path requires `MaestroBoard` setup rows, a pasted
      credential URL, local board selection, or connection CRUD.
- [ ] Every outbound request sends `Authorization: apikey <MAESTRO_API_KEY>` to
      the configured HTTPS Maestro origin, preserving SSRF/private-host guards,
      redirect refusal, bounded errors, timeouts and retry policy.
- [ ] A deployment command validates the configured key, workspace/default-board
      identity, stable integration id and callback URL synchronously after
      install or key rotation; it refuses a key for a different integration when
      local links exist and prints no credential. Callback requests use a fixed
      endpoint and verify HMAC with the configured key.
- [ ] Item creation sends optional remote `board`; omission delegates to the
      server default, and the create response records Maestro's resolved board
      on the local item link.
- [ ] A `MaestroItemLink` belongs to exactly one local Ticket or Incident and
      records the stable remote integration id, remote item id, current remote
      board id, URL and last-sync time. Database constraints prevent duplicate
      reporting of a source and duplicate `(integration_id, remote_item_id)`.
- [ ] `maestro://` is a supported rules handler, reports the Incident
      idempotently, and a linked Incident is protected from resolution deletion,
      pruning and accidental manual deletion.
- [ ] `ticket://` inherits the Incident's group. `board=N` opts into Maestro with
      that remote board; `maestro=1` opts into the default; neither keeps the
      current local-only behavior.
- [ ] Ticket REST exposes `push_to_maestro`, distinguishing boolean `true` from a
      board integer so `true` can never become board id 1.
- [ ] Linked Ticket edits/notes and Incident edits/history sync fail-open through
      jobs. Maestro-origin writes are deduplicated and never echo back.
- [ ] Signed callbacks route by remote item id to Ticket or Incident, append the
      correct note/history, update cached board after a move, and map Maestro's
      canonical lifecycle without depending on board-specific column slugs.
- [ ] Direct Incident merge transfers the sole link when exactly one participating
      Incident is linked and rejects an ambiguous merge with two or more links
      before any partial mutation.
- [ ] Existing `MaestroBoard` / `MaestroBoardLink` rows and encrypted secrets
      remain readable in a deployable legacy state. They are not treated as the
      configured workspace key; an explicit Maestro-confirmed rekey/adoption
      path is required before legacy remote ids become new links.
- [ ] Both documentation tracks explain `django.conf` setup, registration/check,
      default and explicit board routing, Incident-only versus Ticket-plus-
      Maestro flows, manual push, callbacks, permissions and failure behavior.
- [ ] Maestro #32 is re-scoped to workspace integrations/default-board routing
      and its real HTTP tests pass against the pinned django-mojo release before
      either side enables the integration.

### Investigation

- `mojo/apps/incident/models/maestro_board.py` currently creates one encrypted
  credential row per remote board, and `rest/maestro_board.py` exposes setup
  CRUD. That is unnecessary state for a single deployment-wide integration and
  caused `board` to mean a local row id.
- `mojo/apps/incident/models/maestro_board_link.py` links only Ticket + local
  MaestroBoard. Direct Incident reporting needs a source-neutral link; with one
  configured workspace it needs no connection FK, while resolved remote board
  identity belongs on each item link.
- `services/maestro_sync.py` owns the only outbound `requests.post` choke point,
  currently emits `linkkey`, parses a credential-bearing board URL, requires a
  board model argument and builds Ticket-only source payloads.
- `Ticket.on_action_push_to_board` and `TicketHandler` interpret `board` as a
  local model primary key. `TicketHandler` also omits `incident.group` and
  returns early on a cross-incident RuleSet dedupe before any requested push.
- The rule handler registry and `RuleSet.run_handler` allowlist have no
  `maestro` scheme.
- `Incident.on_rest_saved` already records history, but IncidentHistory lacks
  metadata for callback origin/note-id dedupe. Resolution deletion, pruning,
  manual REST deletion and merge can all orphan a direct remote association
  unless each path is addressed.
- The webhook currently selects a `MaestroBoard` by an unguessable path token
  and verifies with that row's encrypted secret. A fixed endpoint plus HMAC with
  the static configured key has the same authentication boundary without
  credential state in the database.
- Maestro #32 currently pins an ApiKey to one board and forbids board moves.
  That contradicts one project-to-workspace integration with a default and
  optional per-report board override.

### Archived Original Description

The item originally requested only replacing `Authorization: linkkey` with
`Authorization: apikey` while preserving a board-bound local model and
server-owned fixed board. That is superseded by the clarified deployment-wide
workspace integration, direct Incident reporting, Ticket-plus-Maestro reporting
and later manual Ticket push.

## Plan

### Objective

Make Maestro a deployment-configured central issue destination rather than a
local board registry. Retain only per-source remote item links, and implement
Incident-only, Ticket-plus-Maestro and manual Ticket reporting with optional
remote board routing and bidirectional updates.

### Implementation

1. **Move the connection to static deployment settings** —
   `mojo/apps/incident/services/maestro_sync.py`, the incident settings
   documentation, and a new incident management command.
   - Read `MAESTRO_API_KEY` and `MAESTRO_API_URL` with `settings.get_static()`;
     default the URL to `https://maestromojo.com`, require HTTPS/public hosts in
     production, and retain the existing development-only HTTP override.
   - Remove runtime dependence on `MaestroBoard`, `paste_url`, `link_key`, cached
     connection schema/status maps and `/api/incident/maestro/board` setup CRUD.
     Never expose the configured key through REST, serializers, logs or command
     output.
   - Add `manage.py register_maestro` (final command name may follow repo naming)
     to POST the derived public callback URL, validate the key, and display only
     safe stable integration id, workspace name/id, default board and status. If
     item links exist, refuse registration when their integration id differs;
     token rotation must be in-place on the same Maestro integration unless an
     explicit ownership migration is requested. No network call occurs during
     app import or ordinary process startup.

2. **Generalize and migrate per-source item links** —
   `models/maestro_board_link.py`, new `models/maestro_item_link.py`, model/REST
   exports and a generated incident migration.
   - Create a `MaestroItemLink` with nullable Ticket and Incident FKs plus a
     database check that exactly one is set. Use `PROTECT` for Incident deletion;
     add partial unique constraints for Ticket and Incident and index the remote
     item id.
   - Persist the non-secret stable integration id returned by Maestro, remote
     board id, URL and last-sync time. Add a unique constraint on
     `(remote_integration_id, remote_item_id)`. Keep creation internal and REST
     exposure read/delete only; unlink stops sync but leaves the remote item.
   - Deploy the new table alongside legacy `MaestroBoard`/`MaestroBoardLink`
     tables. Mark legacy surfaces read-only/inactive rather than converting a
     board key into a workspace key. Provide an explicit adoption command/action
     only after Maestro confirms source-key ownership of each legacy item; do not
     block schema migration or destroy legacy credentials.

3. **Make the wire client source-neutral and workspace-routed** —
   `services/maestro_sync.py` and `asyncjobs.py`.
   - Refactor `_post()` to take no connection model and emit exact `apikey` auth.
     Keep v1/versioning behavior unless Maestro #32 gives the revised contract a
     new version; do not support `linkkey` fallback.
   - Item create accepts `board_id=None`, includes `board` only for a strict
     positive integer and requires Maestro to return the stable integration id
     plus resolved board. Build bounded source data for Ticket or Incident:
     source kind/id, project, URL, title/details, priority and canonical lifecycle.
   - Keep create/update idempotent by local source constraint plus server source
     ownership/idempotency. Update and comment address the remote item id, so a
     same-workspace board move does not sever the route.
   - Replace board/source-specific jobs with source/link ids and optional board
     only on first push. Re-load rows inside jobs; keep 5xx/timeouts retriable,
     4xx terminal, bounded logging and fail-open local saves.

4. **Use a fixed signed callback endpoint** —
   `rest/maestro_webhook.py`, REST registration and `services/maestro_sync.py`.
   - Expose `POST /api/incident/maestro/webhook`, rate-limit it, parse bounded
     JSON and verify `X-Mojo-Signature` with `MAESTRO_API_KEY`. Missing config or
     invalid signatures fail closed without revealing configuration state.
   - Require signed callbacks to carry the stable integration id and resolve
     links by `(integration_id, remote_item_id)`, never item id alone. Ticket comments create
     `TicketNote`; Incident comments create `IncidentHistory`. Add JSON metadata
     to IncidentHistory and thread metadata through `Incident.add_history` for
     `origin`, event and remote-note-id dedupe.
   - Cache board id/URL on move callbacks. Map local resolved/closed to `done`,
     paused/ignored to `parked`, and other statuses to `active`; inbound maps
     those roles to resolved, paused and open using direct compare-before-write
     saves so callback changes never echo.

5. **Add Ticket and Incident reporting hooks** —
   `models/ticket.py`, `models/incident.py`, `models/history.py` and
   `asyncjobs.py`.
   - Replace `push_to_board` with `push_to_maestro`; `true` omits board for the
     server default and a strict positive integer selects a remote board.
     Validate configuration synchronously for manual actions, then queue the
     shared idempotent source push.
   - Enqueue Ticket title/description/status/priority changes and non-Maestro
     notes through its one link. Add corresponding Incident
     title/details/status/priority and IncidentHistory synchronization.
   - Preserve directly linked Incidents during resolution deletion and pruning.
     Reject manual deletion until explicitly unlinked.
   - Make merge transactional and link-aware: transfer and refresh the sole
     direct link when one participating Incident is linked; reject two-or-more
     linked Incidents before events or Tickets move.

6. **Implement rule-driven direct and Ticket reporting** —
   `handlers/event_handlers.py`, `models/rule.py` and handler security tests.
   - Add and register `MaestroHandler`; `maestro://` reports its associated
     Incident to the default and optional `board=N` selects a remote board.
   - Make `TicketHandler` inherit `incident.group` and scope unresolved RuleSet
     dedupe by group. If an eligible Ticket exists, preserve its original
     Incident association, record the new occurrence and idempotently push it
     when this handler requested Maestro.
   - Treat `board=N` as Maestro opt-in plus explicit routing and `maestro=1` as
     default routing. Neither retains existing local-only semantics.
   - Missing config/Incident and malformed selectors produce bounded handler
     failures without deleting local records or blocking event ingestion.

7. **Rewrite integration coverage** —
   `tests/test_maestro_board/test_maestro_service.py`,
   `tests/test_maestro_board/test_maestro_rest.py`, incident handler/retention
   tests, and new command tests.
   - Cover settings lookup/default URL, secret non-disclosure, registration
     command success/failure and wrong-integration refusal, exact `apikey`
     header, fixed webhook signature, integration-namespaced callback routing,
     explicit/default create bodies and resolved-board persistence.
   - Cover constraints/idempotency for both sources, all rule modes, Ticket group
     inheritance, same-group dedupe reuse/push, cross-group separation, manual
     push validation, direct Incident retention/delete/merge behavior, outbound
     changes/comments, callback routing/dedupe/lifecycle/moves, echo suppression,
     revoked credentials and retry/drop behavior.
   - Cover deployable legacy rows and explicit server-confirmed adoption without
     asserting that a legacy key is compatible. Limit HTTP mocks to client
     emission; Maestro #32's real HTTP suite proves auth and routing.

8. **Replace board-bound documentation in both tracks** — current Maestro board
   guides, their indexes and `helpers/settings_reference.md`.
   - Document the `django.conf` settings, file-secret handling, registration
     command, one key per deployment and rotation procedure.
   - Give examples for `maestro://`, local-only `ticket://`, default/explicit
     Ticket reporting and manual `push_to_maestro`.
   - Explain remote board ids, server default, source ownership, callbacks,
     lifecycle mapping, same-workspace moves, retention, permissions, retries and
     the Maestro #32 version dependency. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

9. **Re-scope Maestro #32 before release**.
   - Move creation from Board settings to Workspace Integrations. Each project
     integration has a workspace ApiKey, default board, callback URL and source
     identity; the key's group is the hard tenant boundary.
   - Accept optional board on create, validate it inside the active workspace,
     default server-side when omitted and return the resolved board. Allow human
     moves within that workspace while retaining source-key ownership.
   - Emit current board and canonical lifecycle in signed callbacks. Test many
     project integrations into one workspace, key isolation, default/override
     routing, cross-workspace denial, same-workspace moves and callback signing
     over real HTTP against the pinned django-mojo release.

### Design Decisions

- **Settings, not a connection model**: a singular deployment credential is
  operational configuration. Database state is retained only where cardinality
  exists: one remote item link per reported Ticket or Incident.
- **Server-owned default**: the ApiKey/integration answers which workspace and
  default board; an optional request answers which same-workspace board for one
  report. Local configuration never duplicates routing policy.
- **Remote ids only**: `board=3` is Maestro board 3. A local setup-row id has no
  meaning outside one django database.
- **Explicit Ticket opt-in**: plain `ticket://` remains local. `board` implies
  reporting; `maestro=1` explicitly requests default routing.
- **Direct Incident, not a synthetic Ticket**: use `maestro://` when Maestro is
  the only workflow record; use Ticket reporting when local users need a local
  issue and resolution updates.
- **Fixed callback plus HMAC**: an unguessable database path token is unnecessary
  when every body must verify under the deployment ApiKey. Key rotation requires
  a coordinated activation/restart and re-registration so Maestro and every
  django-mojo process switch together.
- **Stable integration identity**: the ApiKey token may rotate, but its Maestro
  integration id does not. Every local link and callback carries that non-secret
  id, preventing a valid key from another project integration in the same
  workspace from adopting or misrouting existing items.
- **Moves remain valid inside the workspace**: ownership follows integration key
  and item id, not the original board.
- **Canonical lifecycle**: Maestro translates arbitrary board workflow columns
  into `active`/`done`/`parked`; django-mojo never carries per-board status maps.
- **No mixed-contract release**: neither repository enables reporting until
  cross-repo tests pass against pinned versions.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- Missing/blank key: rules log and preserve local records; manual push and the
  registration command return a clear configuration error naming the setting.
- Key values are never present in REST, logs, job logs, exceptions or command
  output. `django.conf` must use deployment-standard secret file permissions.
- Missing board is valid and resolves server-side. An absent/inactive default or
  explicit malformed/cross-workspace/inactive board is a terminal rejection; no
  local link is created and no local board is guessed.
- Concurrent source pushes converge through the local unique constraint and
  Maestro source idempotency.
- `django.conf` is loaded once per process. Key rotation therefore uses an
  explicit maintenance sequence: verify the new token belongs to the same stable
  integration, pause/drain reporting and callbacks, update configuration on all
  nodes, restart web/job workers, run registration, activate the new token, then
  resume. Maestro may provide a bounded old/new acceptance window, but the client
  never silently keeps an unbounded second key. A rolling uncoordinated rotation
  is documented as unsafe because old workers would drop new callbacks/outbound
  requests.
- A same-workspace move updates cached board and continues sync; a cross-workspace
  move remains forbidden.
- Maestro-origin notes/history dedupe remote note ids and never enqueue back.
- Direct Incident deletion is refused while linked. Merge transfers the sole
  link but rejects ambiguity before any partial write.
- Legacy rows remain readable/inactive until explicit server-confirmed adoption;
  schema migration never guesses, blocks startup or destroys encrypted secrets.

### Challenge

| # | Objection | Disposition | Evidence / what changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|-------------------------|
| 1 | RuleSet dedupe returns before a requested Maestro push and can reuse a Ticket from another local group. | **amended** | Dedupe becomes group-scoped; a Maestro-enabled recurrence reuses and pushes the eligible Ticket, records the occurrence and preserves its original Incident relationship. |
| 2 | Manual Incident delete or merge can erase a direct link and orphan its remote item. | **amended** | The link protects Incident deletion; transactional merge transfers one link or rejects two-or-more-link ambiguity before mutations. |
| 3 | Converting/aborting on legacy board credentials can either mis-scope keys or strand deployment. | **amended** | New links deploy alongside readable inactive legacy rows. Only a Maestro-confirmed rekey/adoption converts remote ownership; ordinary migration neither guesses nor blocks. |
| 4 | A replacement ApiKey from another project integration in the same workspace could validate but not own existing remote items. | **amended** | Maestro returns a stable non-secret integration id; registration compares it with existing links and refuses replacement. Normal rotation must preserve that id. |
| 5 | Updating `django.conf` in one process can split web/job workers during rotation and turn valid work into terminal signature/auth failures. | **amended** | Rotation now has a pause/drain, all-node config, restart, register, activate, resume sequence; uncoordinated rolling rotation is explicitly unsupported. |
| 6 | Callback routing by remote item id alone can collide after adoption or accidental integration replacement. | **amended** | Links are uniquely constrained and callbacks routed by `(integration_id, remote_item_id)`. |
